blocks.text: Setting up your Mac for payroll tasks

Since Google Sheets runs in a browser, your Mac experience depends on how you manage your tabs. Open your primary payroll sheet in Google Chrome. Click the three dot menu at the top right. Select Cast, Save, and Share. Choose Install page as app. This creates a shortcut in your Applications folder. You can now launch your payroll sheet like a native Mac app.
Essential spreadsheet tips for payroll accuracy

Data reconciliation is the core of your work. Use the VLOOKUP or XLOOKUP function to compare your payroll software export against your time tracking data. If you see a #N/A error, check if the employee ID format matches in both sheets. Leading spaces often cause these errors. Use the TRIM function to clean your data before running comparisons.

blocks.text: Speed matters when you have a deadline. Press ⌘ + / to open the full list of keyboard shortcuts. Use ⌘ + ⇧ + H to find and replace values. Use ⌘ + ⌥ + 9 to hide rows that are not relevant to the current pay period. These small actions save minutes every hour.

Google Sheets now supports up to 20 million cells. Large files can still be slow if you have too many complex formulas. If your sheet lags, convert static data to values. Select the range, copy it with ⌘ + C, and use Edit > Paste special > Values only. This removes the calculation overhead while keeping your data.

You likely receive over 100 emails a day. Use folders or labels to separate payroll queries from general communication. If you need to research a tax rule, let Lazur handle the search in the background. It will summarize the relevant info so you can stay in your spreadsheet.
When you are stuck in a complex menu, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a specific setting is. It will draw a circle around the menu item for you.
blocks.title: Find menus quickly

blocks.text: Payroll data is sensitive. Always check your sharing settings before sending a file. Use File > Share to ensure only authorized personnel have access. Never leave sensitive sheets open on your screen when you step away from your Mac. Use ⌃ ⌘ Q to lock your screen quickly.
What to do when formulas break

Formula errors are common. A #REF! error usually means you deleted a row or column that the formula needs. A #VALUE! error often means you are trying to do math on text. Check your cells for hidden characters. Sometimes a simple copy and paste into a plain text editor removes these artifacts.

faq.question: Is there an official Google Sheets app for Mac?
faq.answer: No, Google Sheets runs in your web browser. You can create a desktop shortcut in Chrome to make it feel like a standalone app.

faq.question: How do I fix a #REF! error in my payroll sheet?
faq.answer: This error happens when a formula refers to a cell that no longer exists. Check your formula references and update them to point to the correct range.

faq.question: Can I use Lazur to edit my payroll cells?
faq.answer: Lazur cannot click buttons or edit your cells directly. It can guide you through the steps, show you where tools are, or dictate text for you.

faq.question: How many cells can I have in a Google Sheet?
faq.answer: As of September 2026, the limit is 20 million cells per spreadsheet.
